plan.summary: The network layers under every web page: packets, DNS, HTTP and its versions, TLS, URLs and origins, caching, CDNs, compression, cookies, realtime transports and API styles.

prerequisites.bridge: The browser sends a request; the server returns status, headers and body.
A client asks for data; a server listens and answers.
A small block of data with a header that says where it goes.

outcomes: Explain what happens on the network between typing a URL and the first byte of the page.
Explain how DNS resolves a name and choose the right record type and TTL.
Compare HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 and explain head-of-line blocking at each layer.
Explain the TLS 1.3 handshake and the certificate chain of trust.
Configure HTTP caching, CDN caching and compression for a static site with hashed assets.
Set cookies with safe attributes and explain origin versus site.
Choose a realtime transport and an API style for a product feature.

lesson_outline.title: How the internet moves your request: packets, IP, TCP and UDP
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A request becomes packets that cross routers; a sequence diagram shows the hops, the TCP handshake and a resent lost packet.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Order the steps from typing a URL to the first byte arriving.

experience.override_reason: Deep budget is 18; the selector chose interactive (3). The packet journey is one fixed sequence, so a sequence diagram teaches it and keeps the budget for the caching and HTTP version labs.

lesson_outline.title: Domains, DNS resolution and hosting
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The resolver asks root, TLD and authoritative servers in a fixed order; a sequence diagram shows each query, answer and TTL.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Order the resolution chain and pick the record type for each job.

experience.override_reason: Deep budget is 18; the selector chose explainer (2). A sequence diagram shows the same fixed query chain at no cost.

lesson_outline.title: URLs, origins and sites
lesson_outline.visual_reason: One URL splits into scheme, host, port, path, query and fragment; a labelled diagram shows which parts make the origin and which make the site.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Sort URL pairs into same-origin, same-site or cross-site.

lesson_outline.title: HTTP messages: methods, status codes and headers
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A request and its response have fixed parts; an annotated diagram shows the start line, headers and body of each.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Match each situation to its method and status code.

lesson_outline.title: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3: head-of-line blocking
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Head-of-line blocking appears at different layers in each version; the learner drops a packet and watches which streams stall in HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 over TCP and HTTP/3 over QUIC.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Drop one packet and predict which responses stall in each HTTP version.

experience.override_reason: Deep budget is 18; the selector chose hybrid (6). One parameter (which packet is lost) drives the lesson, so an interactive lesson with checkpoints is enough.

lesson_outline.title: TLS and HTTPS: the handshake and the chain of trust
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The TLS 1.3 handshake is a sequence of messages in one round trip; an explainer shows key share, certificate and Finished messages in order.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Order the handshake messages and name what each certificate in the chain proves.

video.reason: The TLS 1.3 handshake is a timed sequence of messages in one round trip; a 60 s explainer shows them in order.

lesson_outline.title: HTTP caching: freshness, revalidation and cache busting
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Cache behavior depends on several headers and on time; the learner changes Cache-Control, ETag and the clock and watches fresh, stale and revalidated responses.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Set Cache-Control directives and predict whether the next request hits the cache, revalidates or goes to the origin.

lesson_outline.title: CDNs and the edge
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A CDN puts caches near users; a diagram shows user, PoP, origin shield and origin, and where the cache key and purge act.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Name which layer answers a request and what a purge removes.

lesson_outline.title: Compression: gzip, Brotli, Zstandard and dictionaries
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The codecs trade compression ratio against CPU time; a side-by-side comparison shows when each fits.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Match each asset and delivery setup to the right compression.

lesson_outline.title: Cookies: attributes, SameSite and prefixes
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Whether the browser sends a cookie depends on its attributes and on the request; the learner changes SameSite, Secure, Domain and the request type and sees when the cookie is sent.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Change the attributes and predict whether a cross-site request carries the cookie.

lesson_outline.title: Realtime transports: polling, SSE, WebSockets, WebTransport and WebRTC
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Choosing a transport is a set of decisions (who sends, how often, peer to peer or not); a branching deck walks the learner through them.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Pick a transport for each product feature and justify it.

lesson_outline.title: REST, GraphQL and RPC in production
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Each API style puts the contract in a different place; a diagram compares one request in REST, GraphQL and RPC and how each uses HTTP caching.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Sort API needs into REST, GraphQL or RPC.

mini_projects.use_case: A developer moving a site to a new host checks that A, AAAA, CNAME, CAA and HTTPS records and their TTLs are right before switching nameservers.
A frontend team checks that hashed assets are immutable and HTML revalidates, by grading Cache-Control, ETag, Vary and Content-Encoding headers from a HAR file.
A security reviewer reads the Set-Cookie headers of a login flow and flags missing Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite and broken __Host- prefixes.

capstone.name: site network report CLI
capstone.problem: Before launch, a team checks a site's network setup; a Node.js CLI reads saved DNS answers, TLS certificate data and HAR responses and reports problems in DNS, HTTPS and HSTS, HTTP version, caching, compression and cookies against a policy.

goals: master frontend engineering end to end from the N1 roadmap
learn visually and by experimenting with simulations

curriculum.scope: The network a frontend developer depends on: internet packets and transport, domains and DNS, HTTP messages and versions, TLS, URLs and origins, HTTP and CDN caching, compression, cookies, realtime transports and API styles at a glance.

concepts.title: IP addresses, IPv4/IPv6 and ports
concepts.reason: No verified source in this run explains IP addressing and ports in depth (HPBN mentions IP only briefly); page 1 names IP addresses and ports inside the packet journey, and the coverage audit may add a source.

concepts.title: Static, server and serverless hosting
concepts.reason: No verified source in this run compares static, server and serverless hosting; the roadmap's deployment and hosting phase teaches it.

concepts.title: DNS prefetch and DNS over HTTPS
Why domain sharding and sprites are anti-patterns now
Certificates, CAs and the chain of trust
Origin versus site and the public suffix list
Vary, browser caches and shared caches
PoPs, origin shield, cache keys and purge
Polling, long polling and Server-Sent Events
Resource-oriented REST
concepts.reason: No verified REST-style source in this run (RFC 9110 defines resources and methods, not the REST style); the roadmap deep-dives REST in Phase 13.
